summary: Road to VR reports that Valve has discontinued the Index PC VR headset (2019) and is selling it and its parts at 20% off. The writer's take is that the sale mainly suits existing owners buying replacement parts, since SteamVR base-station tracking is fading and Steam Frame, Valve's standalone headset, launched last month. The item is a hardware retail and product-lifecycle story with no AI content.
speakers_or_authors: Road to VR staff writer (journalism, XR trade press)
relevance_reason: This is about a legacy PC VR headset being discontinued and discounted. It has no connection to AI agents, personal-context AI, voice interfaces or AI built into operating systems. Steam Frame is mentioned only as a VR/streaming device.

claims.claim: Valve has stopped producing the Index headset and is discounting all Index items by 20 percent.
claims.quote: Valve Index is no longer being produced, which means this could be your last chance to get new stock of the company’s landmark PC VR headset.

claims.claim: The author says the sale suits existing owners seeking cheaper replacement parts rather than newcomers to PC VR.
claims.quote: I’d consider the sale to be more appealing to existing owners hoping to get their hands on cheaper replacement parts than anyone looking to get into the ecosystem right now.

commercial_interest: No sponsorship or investment is disclosed. The discount is Valve's own promotion of its product, reported by a trade publication.
older_event: No. The Index launched in 2019, but the discontinuation and sale are the new news. Steam Frame's release last month is mentioned as context.
